title: Even Dogs Seem to Experience the Mysterious Bouba/Kiki Effect - Nautilus
gist: A Proceedings of the Royal Society B study suggests dogs may experience the bouba/kiki effect, in which sounds map to rounded versus spiky shapes, a phenomenon seen across human cultures and relevant to language evolution.

insights.claim: People across cultures, including those without written language and those blind since birth, tend to link 'bouba' with rounded shapes and 'kiki' with spiky ones.
insights.speaker: Jake Currie
insights.so_what: Evidence for non-arbitrary sound-shape associations in language.
insights.locator: It's also proved to be strikingly widespread.

insights.claim: A new Proceedings of the Royal Society B study indicates the bouba/kiki effect may extend to dogs.
insights.speaker: Jake Currie
entities: Proceedings of the Royal Society B
insights.so_what: Suggests sound-shape mapping may not be uniquely human; the excerpt gives no study details.

insights.claim: The effect is a strong indication that we associate certain sounds with certain shapes, which has implications for the evolution of language.
insights.speaker: Jake Currie
insights.so_what: Informs theories of how language originated.
insights.locator: this particular idiosyncrasy of the human mind
